_sobre: Programs with known compatibility in the WinApps engine. 'match' uses regular expressions (case-insensitive) against: file = file name, product = ProductName/FileDescription/CompanyName of the .exe, content = the file's bytes. Rules are checked in order and the first match wins, so specific rules come before generic ones. Human-readable fields are in ENGLISH: name, summary, why, alt, fixes, category, app_name, and the labels in mac_menu and titlebar_buttons. The optional object 'pt' holds the same keys in Brazilian Portuguese; when the interface language is Portuguese each key there replaces the English one (missing keys fall back to English). status: 'funciona' (works), 'parcial' (partial) or 'nao-funciona' (doesn't work) — identifiers, never translated. 'verified' = tested end to end by WinApps, with the fixes it needs (Verified badge). 'tested' = date of the last test (DD/MM/YYYY). 'fixes' = WinApps fixes the program relies on. 'category' = group in the table. 'kind': 'app' (one program) or 'grupo' (generic rule by technology). 'needs' = components WinApps installs first (winrt-metadata, webview2, dotnet48…). 'app_name' = shortcut name (the program's real product name, normally the same in every language). 'summary' = one-line summary (table); 'why'/'alt' = details when expanded. 'mac_menu' = the program's Mac menus (each item presses one of its keyboard shortcuts); menu '@app' = items in the menu named after the program. 'titlebar_height' = height (points) of the program's own title bar when it is HTML (WebView2) and the engine can't measure it. 'titlebar_buttons' = buttons on the Mac title bar {left, right: [label, action, SF Symbol]}; action = a shortcut ('ctrl+s') or 'click:X,Y' (points from the window's top-left corner; negative X counts from the right) on an item of the hidden title bar; 'click!:X,Y' = a click that opens a window: retried once if none appears. Symbol '@floppy' = floppy disk drawn by WinApps (macOS has none). Menus and title bar buttons are written when the shortcut is created, in the interface language at that moment. COMPATIBILITY.md and COMPATIBILIDADE.md are generated from this file (compat-md.py). User guide: GUIDE.md / GUIA.md.

rules.name: Power BI Desktop
rules.why: Works in the WinApps engine (tested on Nov 7, 2026): reports, Power Query, Analysis Services and visuals. Before installing, WinApps sets up .NET Framework 4.8, the Windows metadata (WinRT) and WebView2. The first launch takes a few minutes.
rules.alt: When it opens, a "Something went wrong" message may appear: just close it. Power BI updates may require a newer version of WinApps.
rules.mac_menu_fonte: Atalhos oficiais: learn.microsoft.com/power-bi/create-reports/desktop-accessibility-keyboard-shortcuts (Salvar/Desfazer/Refazer/Copiar/Colar = atalhos padrão do Windows)
rules.summary: Reports, Power Query, Analysis Services and visuals

rules.name: RubinOT
rules.why: Tested on Nov 8, 2026: login, character on the map, chat, inventory, store and Battle Pass. You can resize the window freely (the game scales with it) and the close button quits the game. The session still drops now and then (the client closes on its own); the watchdog installed with the game reopens the client automatically.
rules.alt: Use the RubinOT.app shortcut; the launcher isn't needed. Installation uses the WinApps recipe (programas/rubinot/install.sh). To stop it from reopening automatically, create a file named .rubinot-sem-vigia in the environment folder.
fixes: Reopens automatically if the session drops
rules.summary: Plays well, but the session drops now and then (reopens automatically)

rules.why: Uses WebView2 (Edge's built-in browser). WinApps installs the WebView2 Runtime if it's missing and draws its screens through Metal.
rules.alt: If a screen stays blank, quit and reopen the program; the first image may take a few seconds.

rules.name: Direct3D 12 game
rules.why: Uses Direct3D 12, which the engine doesn't support on the Mac. Some games have a Direct3D 11 option, which works.
rules.alt: Look for a Direct3D 11 mode in the game's options (or -dx11 on the command line).
rules.summary: No Direct3D 12; use the game's Direct3D 11 mode
